spans.s:
paṇí, m.
 —1. bargainer, who gives nought
without return; chafferer, haggler, and so
 —2. niggard; esp. one who is stingy towards
the gods, an impious person;
 —3. a
malicious demon. [√paṇ.]

pāṇí, m. hand. [prob. for *palni: cf.
παλάμη, Lat. palma, AS. folm, ‘palm,
hand’: radically akin is AS. fēl-an, Eng.
feel.]

paṇḍitá, a. learned; as m. learned man,
Anglo-Indian pandit.

páṇya, grdv. to be bargained for or bartered;
 as n. article of trade. [√paṇ, 963.]

pāṇi-grāha, m. hand-grasper, i. e. (see
89^5N.) husband.

pāṇḍú, a. whitish, pale; as m. Pāndu,
name of a prince of the Lunar Race.
